events.title: Trinity Test: First Atomic Bomb Detonated
events.description: The United States conducted the world's first nuclear weapon test at the Alamogordo Bombing and Gunnery Range in New Mexico, detonating a plutonium implosion device code-named 'Gadget' as part of the Manhattan Project.
events.significance: Marked the beginning of the nuclear age, directly paving the way for the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki and reshaping global geopolitics, warfare, and the Cold War arms race.

events.title: Apollo 11 Launches Toward the Moon
events.description: Apollo 11, carrying astronauts Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin, and Michael Collins, lifted off from Kennedy Space Center in Florida atop a Saturn V rocket at 9:32 a.m. EDT.
events.significance: Began the first crewed mission to land on the Moon, which achieved the goal set by President Kennedy and became a defining moment of human exploration and the Space Race.

events.title: Traditional Start of the Islamic Calendar
events.description: July 16, 622 CE (Julian) is commonly used as the epoch of the Islamic Hijri calendar, associated with the Prophet Muhammad's migration (Hijra) from Mecca to Medina.
events.significance: Established the reference point for the Islamic lunar calendar, still used by Muslims worldwide to determine religious observances.

events.title: Establishment of the District of Columbia as the U.S. Capital
events.description: President George Washington signed the Residence Act, which authorized the creation of a permanent capital on the Potomac River, to be situated in a district not exceeding ten miles square.
events.significance: Laid the foundation for Washington, D.C., resolving a contentious debate over the location of the national capital and shaping the early political compromise between North and South.

events.title: Death of John F. Kennedy Jr.
events.description: John F. Kennedy Jr., his wife Carolyn Bessette-Kennedy, and her sister Lauren Bessette died when the small plane Kennedy was piloting crashed into the Atlantic Ocean near Martha's Vineyard, Massachusetts.
events.significance: The tragedy ended the life of the son of President John F. Kennedy and prompted national mourning, often viewed as another chapter in the Kennedy family's history of public loss.
